message:
The narrow slot keeps the dig inside traction for Black Point-1 (BP-1, meaning crushed basalt lunar simulant).
Plain words: cutting only a 100 mm wide saw kerf 50 mm deep then picking up the side spoil with the wide ladder cuts push to one-third of a full-width blade.
Scaling the BP-1 shallow scraper cut force estimate (E9) at 32.9 N by width gives about 11.0 N from the kerf scaling calc (E64), shown in the narrow-kerf pickup sketch (E65); 11.0 N is about 1 kg weight against 294 N traction, so everyday scale says margin is very comfortable.
This is the narrow-kerf trenching chain loosener (C36) as distant analogy from a ride-on trencher, which maps trencher spoil-row to this light robot.

The pour must be metered, not slumped, to hit the bin blind.
Plain words: a short screw in the hopper floor feeds soil to the rear outlet during tilt so the stream stays centred over the bin mouth.
The screw meters 15.0 kg trips through the 150 mm outlet with pivot at 0.550 m clearing the 0.400 m lip by 0.150 m from the tip dump clearance check (E51); a shoe-box pour controlled like a kitchen auger, not a tipped wheelbarrow.
This is the auger-assisted live-bottom discharge (C37) as distant analogy from a grain combine unloading auger, which maps metered unloading to blind-pour accuracy.

On sources others put up, I confirm Mobility and Deployable Chassis Lead on tipping and qualify the drum power.
Plain words: a raised load behind the axle can tip us, and spinning drums still need power checked against our lamp-bulb budget.
I take from the Skid-Steer Safety for Farm and Landscape (E47) the rule that lifting a load transfers weight and raises the balance point, so I confirm trips stay at 15.0 kg dumped only on level ground for safety factor 1.69; I take from the Single Drum Trench Cutters (E45) the finding that transverse cutters concentrate all power in one drum for tough ground, which from my side means the transverse milling drum loosener (C31) fits traction but must still fit the 16.4 W ladder power from the ladder power estimate (E59), so Power Structure and Integration Lead please keep the fused ladder branch and Autonomy and Blind Operations Lead please keep current-limit backout.
Not ready, because arching plus edge-wear bench tests are still open.
